title: MasterChef India Judge Chef Jolly Opens KASI, a Ganges-Inspired Restaurant, in the New Forest
excerpt: Surjan Singh's first restaurant outside London opens today at Careys Manor in Brockenhurst, pairing a menu that follows the Ganges with Hampshire lamb, chalk-stream trout and Wessex pork.
body:
• KASI, the new Indian restaurant from MasterChef India judge Surjan Singh — Chef Jolly — opens today, Wednesday, November 4, at Careys Manor Hotel & SenSpa in Brockenhurst, in the heart of the New Forest.
  • The menu follows the Ganges from the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal, pairing Indian techniques with Hampshire produce: lamb parantha, banana-leaf trout from the Test and Itchen, Wessex saddleback pork belly with buttered pao.
  • Formats include à la carte, a set thali lunch and three- and five-course tasting menus; bookings are through the hotel.
  • It is Chef Jolly's first restaurant outside London, where he runs The Great Indian in Finsbury Park.

The New Forest gets a new Indian table today. KASI opens at Careys Manor Hotel & SenSpa in Brockenhurst, Hampshire, led by Surjan Singh — better known to MasterChef India viewers as Chef Jolly — in the space formerly occupied by the hotel's French restaurant, Le Blaireau. It is his first restaurant outside London.

A menu that travels the Ganges

KASI takes its name and its map from Varanasi and the cultures along the River Ganges. The menu follows the river from the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal, tracking how ingredients and cooking traditions change along its banks — open-fire cooking, bold spices and historic techniques, with an element of tableside theatre at lunch and dinner.

"The food at KASI will tell the story of the Ganges through the ingredients, flavours and cooking traditions found along its banks. At the same time, it will be firmly connected to its home in the New Forest, making the most of the exceptional produce available locally and across the British Isles."

— Chef Jolly (Surjan Singh)

Indian technique, Hampshire produce

The local sourcing is specific, not decorative. Signature dishes include a Hampshire lamb parantha; banana-leaf-roasted trout from the Rivers Test and Itchen with coriander, garlic and curry leaf butter; roasted Wessex saddleback pork belly with buttered pao buns; and paneer lotus kofta with sundried mint and fennel. Tandoori dishes, biryanis, lentils and fresh breads round out the menu, which runs from à la carte to a set thali lunch and three- and five-course tasting menus, with optional wine and cocktail pairings.

The chef

Chef Jolly has worked in hospitality for more than three decades, across Singapore, Kolkata, Doha and the Maldives, as well as aboard Cunard's Queen Anne, and is known to Indian audiences as a judge on MasterChef India. In London he is behind The Great Indian in Finsbury Park. At KASI, restaurant manager Richard Naulleau — who ran Le Blaireau — stays on to lead the front of house, and the refurbished room trades French formality for earthy colours, deep greens, brass and statement lighting. KASI joins Cambium and Zen Garden as the hotel's third restaurant, open to non-residents as well as guests, for lunch and dinner. Bookings are open through the Careys Manor website. Careys Manor Hotel & SenSpa is on Lyndhurst Road, Brockenhurst, SO42 7RH.
